items.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
items.text: SpriteEffect never creates a MatrixTransform parameter: CacheEffectParameters() looks it up on an effect with no parameters, so matrixParam_ is null and OnApply() returns before computing XNA's orthographic projection with half-pixel offset. XNA 4.0's SpriteEffect exposes MatrixTransform. Sprite projection is supplied by each renderer's SpriteBatch path, so ordinary drawing is unaffected; Parameters["MatrixTransform"] returns null.
items.bible_ref: Bible audit graphics-core-effects E6 (no CNA-BUG id)
items.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/SpriteEffect.cpp (CacheEffectParameters, OnApply); XNA 4.0 IL of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics SpriteEffect ctor (ldstr "MatrixTransform"); tests/SpriteEffectTests.cpp covers only Clone/Apply

items.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
items.text: Only BasicEffect exposes XNA's authentic parameter graph and technique name. AlphaTestEffect (no Texture), DualTextureEffect (no Texture/Texture2), EnvironmentMapEffect (no Texture/EnvironmentMap/DirLight*), SkinnedEffect (no Texture/DirLight*) expose partial hand-built tables and a 'Default' technique where XNA's compiled effects name the technique after the effect ('SpriteBatch' for SpriteEffect); EnvironmentMap/Skinned declare WorldInverseTranspose 4x4 where XNA's .fx declares float3x3, and Bones as 72x4 rows instead of float4x3[72].
items.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/{AlphaTest,DualTexture,EnvironmentMap,Skinned}Effect.cpp (CacheEffectParameters); BasicEffect.cpp (Effect(device,"BasicEffect")); XNA IL CacheEffectParameters strings; modules/renderers/fna3d/effects/*.fxb technique strings; modules/renderers/directx9/src/shaders/xna/{EnvironmentMap,Skinned}Effect.fx

items.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
items.text: ShaderEffect::Clone() does not reject a disposed source (it rebuilds from the retained source strings), while every stock effect and compiled Effect::Clone() throws ObjectDisposedException for a disposed source since SOFTWARE-259.

DIRECTX9 inherits CustomEffects=true and declares neither a shader dialect nor ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT, so the capability profile states that ShaderEffect source does not determine pixels, yet D3D9EffectRenderer compiles caller HLSL (SM2/SM3) and D3D9SpriteBatch executes it; no DIRECTX9 3D draw consumes a custom program.

VULKAN and SDL_GPU report all six ShaderDialect* RendererFeature entries Unsupported because their declared dialect SpirV has no feature entry, although both execute caller SPIR-V; only SupportsShaderLanguageEXT(SpirV, stage) answers truthfully.
The engine layer's capability-name table used in refusal messages lists 18 of the 19 GraphicsCapability members; IndirectDraw is missing, so a refusal on it prints an unrecognised capability name.

items.section: GpuDrawParams: the shared stock-effect draw packet
items.text: GpuDrawParams::specularEnabled (EnvironmentMapEffect's XNA shader-variant switch, true for a non-black specular colour) is filled but read by no renderer, so a specular colour that is black-but-enabled cannot be distinguished from disabled specular.

Capability over-claims recorded by the older draw-path audit (WEBGPU CustomEffects true without an effect renderer; SDL_GPU, SOFTWARE, WEBGPU and HEADLESS MRT/occlusion claims without real paths) no longer match the code: WEBGPU compiles WGSL ShaderEffects, SDL_GPU reports OcclusionQuery false, SOFTWARE and WEBGPU implement MRT and occlusion queries, HEADLESS traces by design.
items.evidence: modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp (SupportsCapability, WebGPUEffectRenderer); SdlGpuRenderer.cpp (SupportsCapability OcclusionQuery false); SoftwareRenderer2DState.cpp (MRT, OcclusionQuery); HeadlessRenderer.cpp

items.section: Answer three: execute compiled Effect Framework bytecode
items.text: Documentation lags the code: the C ABI header effects.h says compiled effects are true only for FNA3D, SDL_GPU, VULKAN and EasyGL and that every other identity reports false (WEBGPU, SOFTWARE, OPENGL4 and DIRECTX9/11/12 also have options); ShaderEffect.hpp's class comment still says 'GLSL-source-based'; GraphicsCapability.hpp says D3D11/D3D12 'can express' compute although both answer false.
METAL refuses ShaderEffect construction (NotSupportedException) and custom-effect 3D draws 'until the adapted renderer has passing macOS shader evidence'; the family cannot be built on Linux CI.

Stock-effect state is captured at draw time: GraphicsDevice calls currentEffect_->FillGpuDrawParams() inside each draw, so a stock-effect property changed after EffectPass::Apply() and before the draw affects that draw, whereas XNA uploads effect state at Apply(). Compiled effects synchronise at Apply() like XNA. Derived from reading; no test pins either behaviour.

CNA-constructed (stock/standalone) EffectParameter records are lenient: SetValue(string) is accepted on non-string records, SetValue(Texture*) fills a generic slot that GetValueTexture2D() does not read, and class/type/shape metadata is not enforced; no focused test covers these lenient-mode paths (compiled-mode type checks are exercised in EffectTests.cpp and CompiledEffectConformance.hpp).

The Bible records PreferPerPixelLighting as an open limitation on SOFTWARE (no lighting engine) and WebGPU SkinnedEffect; at TARGET SOFTWARE has ComputeClassicLighting with a per-vertex/per-pixel switch and WebGPU has a vertex-lit skinned family.

The Bible states CNA evaluates EnvironmentMapEffect's Fresnel term per pixel whereas XNA/FNA evaluate it per vertex; at TARGET the GL corpus and Vulkan compute it per vertex with XNA's COLOR1 saturation clamp.

items.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
items.text: The Bible says ShaderEffect has no public accessor for the compile diagnostic; at TARGET GetCompileErrorEXT(), GetShaderDiagnosticsEXT() and HasRenderer() exist.

items.section: Draw validation has a deliberate order
items.text: Managed draw-range validation is renderer-dependent: EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE opt out (RequiresManagedBufferedDrawRangeValidationEXT false) and forward ranges to the native API as XNA does, so the same out-of-range draw throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException on other renderers only. Architectural decision (SOFTWARE-322), not a defect.
VertexElement::GetHashCode() XORs the four 32-bit fields (zero mapped to INT32_MAX), mirroring XNA's value-type hash; collisions are easy, so it must not serve as a declaration identity.
